extracted.intended_audience: NSF program officers, external peer reviewers, and prospective proposers (principal investigators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for external peer review of National Science Foundation (NSF) full research proposals, including the two NSF merit review criteria and the specific elements reviewers should consider when rating proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual Merit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Intellectual Merit criterion encompasses the potential to advance knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to proposals to assess potential to advance knowledge; reviewers provide written reviews describing strengths and weaknesses in the context of this criterion. Reviewers are asked to consider, for Intellectual Merit, issues such as what proposers want to do, why, how, how success will be judged, and potential benefits. Programs may further interpret this criterion in their solicitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Broader Impacts criterion encompasses the potential to benefit society and contribute to the achievement of specific, desired societal outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied alongside Intellectual Merit; reviewers should evaluate how the proposed activities could benefit society or advance desired societal outcomes. NSF has noted community uncertainty about this criterion and has taken steps (e.g., orientation video) to enhance understanding. Program announcements may specify additional expectations for Broader Impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential to advance knowledge and benefit society (Element 1a/1b)
rubrics_metrics.description: 1a. What is the potential for the proposed activity to advance knowledge and understanding within its own field or across different fields (Intellectual Merit)? 1b. What is the potential for the proposed activity to benefit society or advance desired societal outcomes (Broader Impacts)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This element explicitly maps to both primary criteria and asks reviewers to judge the proposal's expected scholarly contribution and societal outcomes. Applicable examples/metrics include novelty, scope of impact, and plausibility of claimed impacts; data and evidence supporting the asserted impacts should be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity, originality, and potential for transformative concepts (Element 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent do the proposed activities suggest and explore creative, original, or potentially transformative concepts?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess whether the idea is innovative or has the potential to transform a field. Considerations include risk versus reward, whether the proposal departs from incremental advance, and whether the approach opens new avenues of inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan quality and assessment mechanism (Element 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the plan for carrying out the proposed activities well‑reasoned, well organized, and based on a sound rationale? Does the plan incorporate a mechanism to assess success?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess methodological rigor, clarity of objectives, workplan feasibility, milestones, evaluation metrics, and explicit success criteria or assessment methods. Weak or vague plans, lack of risk mitigation, or absence of success metrics are negative indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications of the individual, team, or organization (Element 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: How well qualified is the individual, team, or organization to conduct the proposed activities?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should evaluate PI and team track records, expertise alignment with the proposed work, prior accomplishments, institutional support, and demonstrated ability to manage the project. Consider whether the team composition matches the project's interdisciplinary or technical needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of resources (Element 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there adequate resources available to the PI (either at the home organization or through collaborations) to carry out the proposed activities?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess availability and sufficiency of facilities, equipment, collaborations, institutional support, and budget realism. Consider whether collaborations materially add necessary capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program‑specific additional review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs may have additional review criteria particular to the goals and objectives of the program; all relevant review criteria are described in the program announcement or solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must apply any solicitation- or program-specific criteria in addition to the two NSF criteria. Program officers and solicitations should clearly state such criteria (e.g., education/outreach components, partnership requirements, regional priorities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and substance of reviewer written reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should describe the strengths and weaknesses of proposals in the context of the NSB merit review criteria and provide a documented rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF and COVs evaluate whether reviews provide substantive explanatory comments and documented rationale. High-quality reviews explain scoring, identify specific strengths/weaknesses, and provide constructive feedback useful to PIs and program officers. Increasing written comment quality was identified as a key improvement area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection, qualifications, diversity, and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are chosen for specific types of expertise and POs are required to seek diverse representation among reviewers; new POs must complete training (e.g., unconscious bias, portfolio balance, communications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess reviewer panels for appropriate expertise coverage, demographic and institutional diversity, and absence of conflicts. NSF requires program officers to recruit diverse reviewer panels and has instituted training (including unconscious bias) for new POs. COVs appraise reviewer qualifications as part of oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimization of bias and conflicts of interest; open‑minded deliberations
rubrics_metrics.description: Merit review is designed so deliberations are open‑minded and thoughtful, with biases and conflicts minimized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processes must include conflict-of-interest screening, procedures to reduce unconscious bias, and safeguards to ensure fair treatment of proposers. Reviewers and staff should take orientation materials and follow PAPPG guidance to reduce bias in evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic considerations: portfolio balance and funding constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Program officers make funding recommendations after scientific, technical and programmatic review and consideration of appropriate factors, such as portfolio balance and the amount of funding available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions are not solely based on reviewer ratings; POs consider strategic portfolio composition, risk balance across projects, directorate priorities, and budgetary constraints. Caution is advised to ensure panel composition or review method does not inadvertently bias portfolio-level risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness (proposal dwell time)
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF's performance goal is to inform at least 75% of PIs of funding decisions within six months of receipt of their proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor and report percent of proposals processed within six months. FY2018 result was 72%. Time-to-decision is a metric of process efficiency and proposer service and may be affected by review method, complexity, or program timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of external review (panel-only, ad hoc + panel, ad hoc-only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Most proposals are externally reviewed by panel only, ad hoc reviewers plus a panel, or ad hoc reviewers only; choice of method affects expertise coverage and outcomes (in FY2018: 69% panel only, 22% ad hoc+panel, 5% ad hoc only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select review method appropriate to the proposal portfolio and required expertise. NSB encouraged analysis of the trend toward panel-only reviews and cautioned about unintended impacts (e.g., gaps in expertise leading to inappropriate ranking). COVs sometimes recommended more ad hoc reviewers to fill gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internally reviewed or exempt proposal categories (e.g., EAGER, RAPID, SGER, RAISE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximately 5% of proposals fall into categories exempt from external review and may be internally reviewed only (including EAGER, RAPID, small grants, and some RAISE proposals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal review is used for time-sensitive or exploratory proposals; these mechanisms often have different expectations and in some cases higher funding rates. Program officers should document rationale for internal review and ensure appropriate oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer workload and number of reviews per proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: On average, NSF proposals are reviewed by 3–5 reviewers depending on review method; mean reviews per proposal is tracked by directorate and review method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure adequate number of qualified reviewers to cover technical and broader-impact assessments without overburdening reviewers. Tables in the digest (e.g., mean number of reviews per proposal) are used to monitor workload and review thoroughness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oversight and advisory mechanisms (COVs, advisory committees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Committees of Visitors (COVs) and directorate advisory committees provide external expert judgments on program operation quality, integrity, program-level technical and managerial matters, program management and portfolio balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COVs review processes at ~4–5 year intervals and evaluate integrity and efficiency of proposal review and decision-making; their findings inform NSF management and improvements. Advisory committees provide periodic portfolio and policy advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilots and process improvements evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF pilots (e.g., no-deadline submissions, virtual panels, reviewer orientation video) and investments in submission/review infrastructure are evaluated for effectiveness and impact on review quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSB expects formal analysis of pilot outcomes (e.g., no-deadline pilot surveys) and monitoring of trends (e.g., increase in panel-only reviews). Process changes should be assessed for unintended consequences on reviewer recommendations, expertise coverage, or portfolio risk.
